 Expanding the market for agricultural products through digital solutions.
 VTV.vn - Son La province is supporting farmers, cooperatives, and businesses in bringing agricultural products to digital platforms, opening up more sales channels, and accessing markets.
 Đài truyền hình Việt Nam • 08/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Bringing agricultural products to buyers through digital platforms. 
 In Yen Chau commune, Son La province, Bao Gia 26 Co., Ltd. is bringing its black garlic products to customers in many provinces and cities through e-commerce platforms. The company has built stores on TikTok Shop, Shopee, and Lazada and uses social media to promote and introduce its products.
 The company currently has 20 black garlic processing facilities, with a capacity of over 10 tons of product per year. Investing in processing helps the business develop products with a long shelf life, facilitating packaging, transportation, and online sales.
 Mr. Nguyen Van Tuan, Director of Bao Gia 26 Co., Ltd., shared that approximately 90% of the company's products are currently sold through digital platforms. Expanding this sales channel helps the company reach customers in many localities, reducing its dependence on traditional distribution channels.
 Instead of simply introducing products through distributors, businesses can directly provide information, communicate with buyers, and receive orders. However, to maintain this sales channel, the company must ensure product quality, organize packaging and delivery, and fulfill its commitments to customers. 
 People in Son La are livestreaming to introduce, promote, and sell agricultural products on digital platforms, expanding their product distribution channels.
 In Phiêng Khoài commune, Sơn La province, Kiên Cường Cooperative is also combining quality-standardized production with the promotion and sale of agricultural products in the digital environment.
 The cooperative currently produces nearly 90 hectares of plums and over 60 hectares of Tai Nung pears according to VietGAP standards, with an organic orientation. In addition to traditional distribution channels, the unit has launched its products on the sonla.sanviet.vn platform, utilized social media, and organized livestream sessions directly from the growing areas.
 Ms. Nguyen Thi Nguyet, Deputy Director of Kien Cuong Cooperative, recalled the early days of selling through livestreaming, when members were hesitant and unfamiliar with introducing products in front of the camera. Through a learning process, the cooperative gradually developed a suitable way of introducing products, proactively communicating with customers about product quality, characteristics, and production areas.
 Kien Cuong Cooperative has implemented QR code traceability labels on its products supplied to the market. Information about the growing region and production process is used to introduce and help customers understand the origin of agricultural products.
 For local specialty products, Son La province is focusing on combining brand development, traceability, and trade promotion with the One Commune One Product (OCOP) program.
 According to Mr. Tran Dung Tien, Deputy Director of the Department of Agriculture and Environment of Son La province, the province currently has 210 OCOP products with valid certification, including 1 national-level 5-star product, 59 4-star products, and 150 provincial-level 3-star products.
 You may also like In the period 2026-2030, the agricultural sector has decided not to pursue the quantity of recognized and ranked products, but to focus on developing OCOP (One Commune One Product) along the value chain. According to Mr. Tran Dung Tien, quality, preservation, processing, market maintenance, and product value are key requirements that need to be considered in the development of Son La's distinctive products.
 Supporting digital skills, opening markets from the grassroots. 
 Not only businesses and cooperatives, but also remote mountainous areas are being brought to sell their products, where people previously mainly sold agricultural products through traders or regular customers.
 The village of Phiêng Lương, Gia Phù commune, Sơn La province, has 144 households with 653 inhabitants, all of whom are Dao ethnic minority people. The hilly terrain and scattered population make transporting agricultural products difficult. The people mainly engage in small-scale agriculture and livestock farming, with limited access to markets outside the local area.
 To support local people in promoting and selling their products, the Vietnam Fatherland Front Committee of Gia Phu commune, in coordination with other organizations, organized a livestream program called " Going to the village to finalize orders ". 
 Image source: Vietnam Fatherland Front Committee of Gia Phu Commune, Son La Province.
 Through Facebook, locals directly introduce the distinctive products of Phiêng Lương such as local pork, black chicken, stream fish, smoked meat, and upland rice; they interact with customers and receive orders right during the live broadcast.
 Ms. Cam Ngoc Thu Phuong, Chairwoman of the Vietnam Fatherland Front Committee of Gia Phu commune, said that the locality chose livestreaming in the village to allow people to directly participate in introducing agricultural products and become familiar with selling on digital platforms. Through this activity, people are encouraged to proactively promote their products and find more customers.
 For many households in Phieng Luong, selling goods through social media is still a new concept. Participating in the program, residents are guided on how to select products, film videos, introduce products, and communicate with customers.
 Mr. Dang Van Ninh from Phieng Luong village shared: "Initially, I was hesitant, but the hands-on experience made me more confident." Through the guidance of officials who introduced the products and filmed sales videos, he and other participating households have gained a better understanding of how to approach customers and hope for more similar programs so that the village's agricultural products can reach a wider audience.
 According to trade promotion data, 70 OCOP products and distinctive local agricultural products have been uploaded to the buudien.vn platform; 60 products have been introduced on the sonla.sanviet.vn platform. In addition, 50 typical products from 42 businesses and cooperatives have been promoted on the Son La Provincial Trade Promotion Portal. 
 Image source: Vietnam Fatherland Front Committee of Gia Phu Commune, Son La Province.
 You may also like Mr. Dao Van Quang, Deputy Director of the Son La Provincial Center for Investment, Trade and Tourism Promotion, informed that the unit is coordinating with relevant agencies to organize training and support for farmers, cooperatives and businesses to improve digital business skills, especially livestreaming and selling on e-commerce platforms.
 Along with skills training, support activities also focus on building online stores, refining product descriptions, promoting brands, and connecting with distribution channels. These are essential tasks for businesses, cooperatives, and individuals to maintain online business operations and gradually expand their markets.
 According to Mr. Nguyen Dinh Viet, Chairman of the People's Committee of Son La province, in implementing Resolution 57-NQ/TW of the Politburo and Resolution 71/NQ-CP of the Government, the province has determined that the effectiveness of applying science and technology and digital transformation must be evaluated by concrete results in production, business, and people's lives.
 The key criteria include productivity, production costs, product quality, traceability, market expansion, and producer income. For e-commerce, the requirements are not only to bring agricultural products onto platforms but also to improve sales efficiency, ensure product quality, and maintain customer trust.
